messages:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about landing a small ‘bridge’ primitive that sits between SDK iterator surfaces and the transport. Goal: explicit backpressure + lightweight resume tokens so transports can be simple and languages can expose ergonomic idioms. PR + doc sketch incoming.

maya: Nice. Can you sketch how this differs from the current resume-token + iterator approach?

alex: TL;DR: current model mixes paging/cursor semantics with transport streaming. Problems: retries leak into surface, language ergonomics diverge (py async iter vs ts async iterable vs go channels), and backpressure semantics are implicit. Bridge idea:
- Bridge owns transport handshake, KV cache, and resume token glue.
- Surface (Python/TS/Go) gets a StreamHandle with pull(), cancel(), and a tiny resume_token blob.
- Retry policy lives one layer above transport, can be per-request or per-item depending on idempotency header.

rishi: I like separation. Two concerns: 1) per-item retries vs per-page retries — do we let bridge retry items or only whole pages? 2) Idempotency tokens need to be propagated from SDK surface to transport.

jamie: Language notes:
- Python: async iterator + await handle.pull() maps nicely. We need a sync iterator fallback for blocking usage.
- TS: async iterable push/pull differences mean we should offer both pull() and an async generator wrapper.
- Go: channel + context cancellation is idiomatic — bridge should expose a Context-aware Pull(ctx) and a Channel adapter.

maya: On retries: suggest bridge defaults to per-page retries with pluggable per-item retry hooks. That keeps transports simple and lets workloads opt into finer-grained semantics. Also: surface should be able to mark calls as "idempotent" or provide an idempotency key.

alex: Agreed. Proposed APIs (sketch):
```
// StreamHandle (language-agnostic conceptual)
pull(opts) -> {items: [...], resume_token: "..."}   // backpressure, explicit fetch
cancel() -> void
get_resume_token() -> string | null
```
Wrappers: Python async iterator calls pull() under the hood; TS exposes async generator + pull(); Go exposes Pull(ctx) and Channel() helper.

rishi: Implementation detail: transports should surface a compact resume blob (opaque bytes) that the bridge stores and passes back to surface. That lets us change transport internals without breaking SDKs. Also add a small checksum/version to the blob for migrations.

jamie: Observability: expose per-pull latency + retry_count + bytes_served to Console. That lets Optimize recommend batching/quantization changes.

deploy-bot: Link to RFC follow-up doc: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/bridge-iterator-175 (internal) :link:

alex: Next steps: I'll open a PR with the API sketches and a Python prototype adapter. Would love volunteers for TS/Go adapter experiments. Proposed deprecation: keep old iterator surface for 3 months after stable release, then opt-in flag. Thoughts? :+1:

maya: +1 from me. I'll volunteer for TS adapter.

rishi: I can take Go channel adapter. Will test per-item retry hook with idempotency header flow.

alex: Awesome — assigning self (proto), maya (ts), rishi (go). Will post PR number shortly and a short migration guide.

jamie: Quick nit: ensure we have a migration path for existing resume tokens — maybe bridge can accept legacy token formats and emit new ones during first resume.

alex: Good call. Will add compatibility layer in the bridge. Thanks all.
